headline: Iran Diplomacy Pivot Steadies Oil, Sets a Cautious Tone for Monday's Open
body_html:
Markets head into Monday with a notably calmer geopolitical backdrop after President Trump stepped back from a planned strike on Iran and signaled that nuclear talks would commence today, with no deadline imposed for a deal. Crude prices fell sharply on the news, unwinding a portion of the risk premium that had built up through the conflict, while gold edged higher as investors balanced relief with residual uncertainty. The yen also firmed following reported intervention, adding a currency dimension to an already complex macro picture.

Friday's session — the last trading day of July — closed on a mixed note across the 519-stock universe tracked by this desk. Advancers held a narrow edge at 273 to 246, but the sector scorecard was uneven: Energy led with a gain of 1.64%, Software and Industrials added 0.89% and 0.71% respectively, while Homebuilders dropped 1.72% and Healthcare shed 0.97%. Single-stock swings were dramatic, with Roblox tumbling 26.85% and MasTec falling 18.91% among the sharpest declines.

At the open, traders will be watching whether softening oil prices translate into durable equity support or simply compress Energy's recent outperformance. Labor-market sentiment remains a secondary undercurrent after fresh commentary pointed to growing workforce discouragement — a data point worth monitoring ahead of this week's scheduled economic releases.

briefs.headline: Trump Pulls Back Strike on Iran, Opens Door to Nuclear Negotiation
briefs.body: President Trump confirmed over the weekend that a military strike on Iran had been called off in favor of diplomatic engagement, with talks expected to begin Monday. No deadline was attached to the initiative. The pivot caught markets off-guard and sent crude prices meaningfully lower in overnight trading, easing a key source of recent volatility.

briefs.headline: Oil Slides as Deal Hopes Displace Conflict Premium
briefs.body: Brent crude retreated sharply after the Iran strike cancellation, with reports of Saudi tankers resuming Red Sea transit over the weekend adding to supply-relief sentiment. Analysts caution the reprieve may be temporary — commentary circulating over the weekend argued that any Iran-linked refining windfall is likely to prove short-lived once diplomatic progress solidifies.

briefs.headline: Roblox Suffers Steepest Single-Day Drop in the Universe at –26.85%
briefs.body: The gaming platform was Friday's worst performer by a wide margin, sliding nearly 27% in the session to rank as the heaviest decliner in the tracked universe. The move dragged on the broader Internet and consumer-facing segment. No acquisition or merger activity was cited; earnings-related disappointment appeared to be the primary driver.

briefs.headline: DexCom Surges Nearly 12%, Leads Healthcare Devices Higher
briefs.body: DexCom was the top gainer across the universe on Friday, advancing 11.95% and bucking a broader Healthcare sector decline of 0.97%. The move stood out given the sector-wide pressure, suggesting company-specific catalysts — likely tied to quarterly results — drove the outperformance rather than any macro tailwind.

briefs.headline: Eaton and SPX Technologies Propel Industrials to a 0.71% Sector Gain
briefs.body: Electrical-equipment maker Eaton rose 7.32% and HVAC-focused SPX Technologies climbed 10.20%, powering Industrials to one of Friday's stronger sector finishes. The pair's simultaneous surge points to broad-based demand signals within capital-equipment markets, a trend worth tracking as infrastructure spending headlines continue to circulate.

briefs.headline: Workforce Discouragement Adds a Soft Undercurrent to the Labor Outlook
briefs.body: Fresh commentary over the weekend highlighted a growing cohort of workers stepping away from job searches entirely, citing sustained market fatigue as the primary reason. While no hard data release accompanied the discussion, the qualitative signal arrives ahead of a week in which labor-market conditions are expected to remain a focal point for rate-sensitive investors.
